content: High-contention seat/resource reservation systems (Ticketmaster-style) use a 3-state lifecycle AVAILABLE -> HELD -> CONFIRMED. Holds are placed via atomic primitives (Redis SETNX or a Lua script, or a DB row-level lock / conditional UPDATE) so exactly one concurrent writer wins; holds carry a TTL (~5 min) enforced by the store itself (Redis expiry) rather than a background sweeper, and expire back to AVAILABLE lazily. The DB only needs to durably record the CONFIRM write; the hold layer absorbs contention.
